title: generateCode() produces a 6-character code from consonants only
description: Project.generateCode (project.model.js) builds the projectCode from a fixed 21-consonant alphabet ('BCDFGHJKLMNPQRSTVWXYZ') specifically so no vowels can ever appear — the comment states this makes profanity formation structurally impossible, not filtered after the fact.
steps: Call Project.generateCode() 1000 times
Assert every returned value is exactly 6 characters
Assert every character in every value belongs to the set 'BCDFGHJKLMNPQRSTVWXYZ'
expectedResult: All generated codes are 6 characters long and contain only consonants from the defined alphabet — no vowels, digits, or symbols ever appear.

title: createWithCode() retries on projectCode collision up to 5 times
description: projectSchema.statics.createWithCode (project.model.js) catches a Mongo duplicate-key error (code 11000) specifically on the projectCode unique index and retries with a freshly generated code, up to MAX_RETRIES=5, before giving up.
preconditions: Project.generateCode is stubbed to return a colliding code for the first 2 calls, then a unique code
steps: Insert a project with projectCode 'BCDFGH' directly
Stub generateCode to return 'BCDFGH' twice, then 'JKLMNP'
Call Project.createWithCode({ name: 'Retry Test', organizationId })
expectedResult: The document is saved successfully on the 3rd attempt with projectCode 'JKLMNP'; no error is thrown to the caller for the first two collisions.

title: createWithCode() throws after exhausting all 5 retry attempts
steps: Stub Project.generateCode to always return the same already-taken code
Call Project.createWithCode({ name: 'Always Collides', organizationId })
expectedResult: After exactly 5 attempts, the call rejects with 'Unable to assign a unique project code — please try again' rather than retrying indefinitely.

title: assertOrgAccess() unwraps a populated organizationId subdocument before comparing
description: assertOrgAccess (project.controller.js) does `entity.organizationId?._id ?? entity.organizationId` because getById populates organizationId to { _id, name } for display — comparing the populated object directly via .toString() would yield '[object Object]' and never match req.orgId, silently denying every legitimate same-org request.
preconditions: A project whose organizationId is populated as { _id, name }
steps: Build a project object with organizationId populated to { _id: orgA, name: 'Org A' }
Call assertOrgAccess(project, { orgId: orgA, permissions: new Set() })
expectedResult: No exception is thrown — the populated subdocument's _id is correctly unwrapped and matches req.orgId.

title: buildOrgScope() returns null (unrestricted) only for a super admin with no orgId query param
description: buildOrgScope (project.controller.js) is the org-scoping helper behind /projects (list) and /projects/stats. A non-super-admin always gets req.orgId regardless of any query param they pass.
steps: Call buildOrgScope({ permissions: new Set(['organization.admin']), query: {} , orgId: 'ownOrg' })
Call buildOrgScope({ permissions: new Set(['organization.admin']), query: { orgId: 'targetOrg' }, orgId: 'ownOrg' })
Call buildOrgScope({ permissions: new Set([]), query: { orgId: 'targetOrg' }, orgId: 'ownOrg' })
expectedResult: First call returns null (unscoped, admin browsing all orgs). Second call returns 'targetOrg'. Third call (non-admin) returns 'ownOrg' regardless of the query param supplied — a non-admin can never widen or redirect their own org scope via the query string.

title: CreateProjectModal validateForm() rejects project name outside 2-200 characters
steps: Set formData.name to a single character 'A' and call validateForm()
Set formData.name to a 201-character string and call validateForm()
Set formData.name to a valid 10-character string and call validateForm()
expectedResult: First two calls return false and populate errors.name with 'Project name must be between 2 and 200 characters'; the third call returns true with no error.

title: CreateProjectModal validateForm() rejects an end date on or before the start date
steps: Set timeline.startDate = '2026-08-10' and timeline.endDate = '2026-08-10' (same day)
Call validateForm()
Set timeline.endDate = '2026-08-09' (before start) and call validateForm() again
expectedResult: Both calls return false with errors.endDate = 'End date must be after start date'; a genuinely later end date passes validation.

title: calculateProgress() returns 0 without dividing by zero when a project has no milestones
description: The project list page's calculateProgress helper divides completed milestone count by total milestone count — must guard the empty-array case explicitly rather than producing NaN in the Progress bar.
steps: Call calculateProgress({ milestones: [] })
Call calculateProgress({ milestones: undefined })
Call calculateProgress({ milestones: [{status:'Completed'}, {status:'Not Started'}] })
expectedResult: First two calls return 0 (not NaN). Third call returns 50.

title: getCreationRequestId() rejects an Idempotency-Key header longer than 200 characters
steps: Call getCreationRequestId(req) where req.get('Idempotency-Key') returns a 201-character string
Call getCreationRequestId(req) where the header is an empty/whitespace-only string
Call getCreationRequestId(req) where the header is a normal 36-character UUID
expectedResult: First call throws AppError.badRequest('Idempotency-Key must be between 1 and 200 characters'). Second call also throws (normalizes to empty, treated as invalid). Third call returns the trimmed UUID string.
